messages.subject: compatibility with eDMR
parts:
Hi, 
Thanks for the new methylKit, the speed has improved. 
But I am getting error when I am passing over the output from calculateDiffMeth to eDMR. 

So my code is given below. 
"""

> myDiff=calculateDiffMeth(meth)
> source("http://edmr.googlecode.com/files/eDMR.v.0.4.R")
> myDMR=eDMR(myDiff,step=100,dist="none",DMC.qvalue=0.01,DMC.methdiff=25,num.DMCs=1,num.CpGs=3,DMR.methdiff=20,plot=FALSE,main="example",mode=1)

[1] "DMR analysis for all detected CpGs..."
number of iterations= 233
[1] 69.3902

Error in `[.data.frame`(input, idx, 4:8) : undefined columns selected

"""

I was curious whether data structure has changed with the update. 
Thanks,

Jawon

Sheng,

It may just be me, but I have updated my code to use methylKit v0.9.1 and am also working with your eDMR v0.5.1 amd am still having a few issues.

From what I can tell, the eDMR input code still requires "strand"...which is no longer part of the methylDiff object from methylKit. As a crude fix, I simply assigned strand information so that eDMR will read the object in:
myDiff$strand <- rep("+",nrow(myDiff)) #with new methylKit, add strand info

....however, even upon doing this I am still getting nothing but "NaN" for DMR.pvalue and DMR.qvalue [see below]

Any thoughts as to what could be going on?

Thanks,
Shannon

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] compatibility with eDMR
parts:
Hi Shannon,
new objects in methylKit should have the strand information. Only change is that we dropped the id column. if you run the example you will see that it returns the strand.
data(methylKit)

my.diffMeth=calculateDiffMeth(methylBase.obj,slim=TRUE,weigthed.mean=TRUE,num.cores=1)
Let me know if you figure out why or in which cases it drops the strand column.

Best,
Altuna
